title: The verification the unarmed warning recommends cannot see the faces the pipeline's own certificate rejects
body: **What we found.** The warning `grid_pipeline` prints when the winding gates are not armed names `wind_audit`'s FULL TURN test as the way to verify the result. That check passes while the pipeline's own certificate does not, and the faces the certificate rejects reach the delivered sheet. The certificate per cube, with the axis table and with one constant centre, over the 1,728 cubes of the window. **Why it matters.** The two tests do not look at the same thing. FULL TURN looks for a component whose turn count closes a whole wrap; the faces in question reach 0.366318 of a wrap at the largest, where a full turn fusion would be near 1.0. So no full turn test can see them, and a user who follows the warning is told a run is clean when the pipeline would refuse part of it. **That it is not the scroll centre we chose.** The window was certified twice, once with the axis table it was meshed with and once with one constant scroll centre. Both readings find faces the certificate rejects and both find FULL TURN at zero, so the disagreement is between the two tests and not between two ways of placing the axis. The two readings do not even agree with each other, and not in one direction: four cubes the constant centre flags are clean under the table, and one it calls clean carries three under it. **The numbers**, on a 27 cube window of PHerc. 0139 with `--grow-wind-tol 0`, which is both the compiled default and what the warning recommends: | reading of the axis | FULL TURN fusions | faces the certificate rejects at 0.30 | cubes carrying them, of 27 | max abs dw | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | the axis table the window was meshed with | 0 | 3 | 1 | 0.366318 | | one constant scroll centre | 0 | 26 | 4 | 0.476326 | Each row is the same on the mesh geometry and on the placed geometry, so nothing is removed between the mesher and the strip. The count that belongs in a report is the one the pipeline itself applies, which is the first row. **How to check it yourself.** Mesh a window with `--grow-wind-tol 0`, run `wind_audit` on it and read FULL TURN, then run `pipeline_count_winding_shortcut_faces` at tolerance 0.30 on the same cubes. The first says zero and the second does not. --- When the winding gates are not armed, `grid_pipeline` prints a warning that tells the user how to arm them and how to check the result: ``` *** Arm it: --umb-y 3405 --umb-x 2878 --wrap-pitch 9.5 *** --grow-wind-tol 0 (keeps the certificate, *** disables only the over-splitting BPA gate) *** Verify with wind_audit: FULL-TURN must be 0. ``` We followed it, on a 27 cube window of PHerc0139 with the axis and pitch of that scroll. **The check it names passes and the pipeline's own certificate does not**, and the faces the certificate rejects reach the delivered sheet. ## What we measured With `--grow-wind-tol 0`, which is both the compiled default (`grid_pipeline.c:305`) and what the warning recommends: | what | with the axis table the window was meshed with | with one constant scroll centre | |---|---|---| | `wind_audit` FULL TURN fusions, the check the warning names | **0** | **0** | | faces `pipeline_count_winding_shortcut_faces` rejects at 0.30 | **3** | **26** | | cubes carrying them, of 27 | **1** | **4** | | max abs dw over the window | 0.366318 | 0.476326 | **The two readings do not agree, and not in one direction either.** The four cubes the constant centre flags are **clean** under the table; a fifth cube the constant centre calls clean, `z09216_y02432_x02560`, carries **3** under it. The `_mesh.obj` and `_placed.obj` geometries give the same count cube for cube, so nothing is removed between the mesher and the strip in either reading. FULL TURN fusions are **0 on every row of both** (`growth-gate-cost/evidence/placed-certificate-axis.csv` for the table reading and `placed-certificate.csv` for the constant one; the audit's own column is `full_turn_fusions` of `evidence/wind-audit.csv`). The count that belongs in a report is the one the pipeline itself applies, and that is the table: **3 faces on 1 cube of 27**. We are telling you the other number too, because the difference between them is the point of the last remedy below. ## Why the two disagree, which we think is the whole of it They measure different things and the warning points at the weaker one. `wind_audit`'s FULL TURN test looks for a component whose turn count closes a whole wrap, and the faces the certificate rejects here do not: their `max |dw|` is 0.366318 at the largest, where a face bridging turn N to turn N+1 would be near 1.0. They are not full turn fusions and no full turn test can see them. They are the smaller winding errors the certificate exists to catch, and `--grow-wind-tol 0` leaves them in while the recommended verification says the run is clean. **One measurement we had and have withdrawn.** An earlier draft added that those faces span about 0.34 of a wrap pitch. That figure was computed over the **26** faces of the constant centre reading, and we cannot recompute it over the **3** the axis table gives, because the tool that writes the per face radii, `src/tools/sa_bad_faces.c` in our tree, takes a constant umbilicus and not the table. That is the same limitation as remedy 3 below, met from the other side, and we would rather drop a number than carry one measured on the other reading's faces. ## What we are not saying We are **not** saying the gate should be armed by default. `grid_pipeline.c:300` explains why it is not: on PHerc0139 the growth gate fragments ordinary sheets, 10 charts to 68 or more on the canonical fixture, and we see the same, 9 charts against 141 on one cube. Arming it has a real cost and the comment is right to call it research only. We are also aware that a winding guard in this repository has already made a consumer worse: **#13** is kept in draft by its own author because the complete RAW five stage consumer regressed, multi cover 50.96 to 57.78 per cent against a 0.20 point safety limit. That is a reason to be careful with any remedy here, including ours. ## What we think would help, in order of how cheap it is 1. **Change the verification line in the warning.** `wind_audit` FULL TURN is not a sufficient check for what `--grow-wind-tol 0` leaves. The pipeline already computes the stronger one; if the warning named the certificate's own count instead, a user following it would see the 26. 2. **Say in the warning that the certificate can reject faces that then ship.** One sentence. The present text reads as though the certificate being kept is enough. 3. **Say that the count depends on the centre, and have the warning name the axis table.** This is the one we would put first if we had measured it before writing. The same 27 cubes, the same certificate code, the same tolerance: **3 rejected faces on 1 cube** when the certificate is given the axis table the window was meshed with, **26 on 4 other cubes** when it is given one constant centre. A user who runs the check with a constant centre, which is the easy thing to do, gets a number that is wrong in both directions. If the tool that reports this took the axis table the way `cube_mesh` takes it, the question would not arise. 4. If it is useful to you, we can post the per face table: cube, face index, the dw, the radial span and the edge lengths, for either reading. Happy to turn any of this into a pull request in whatever form fits.
